note: English renderings of the meaning, not the Arabic wording. Every entry names its collection and hadith number so it can be looked up independently - an entry whose number could not be confirmed is not included at all. Nothing here is paraphrased for effect or attributed loosely. Entries outside Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim carry a grading (al-Albani for Sunan Abi Dawud, Darussalam for Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Sunan an-Nasa'i); where two collections are graded differently the lower grade is recorded, and nothing graded weak is included. References were checked against sunnah.com. An entry with no 'prayers' list is about prayer generally and is shown in every period; the rest name the prayer they are actually about, because linking a narration to a prayer it never mentions - only to reach a count - would be the same error as inventing one.

hadith.text: Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter Paradise.
Angels take turns among you by night and by day, and they gather together at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.
Whoever catches one rak'ah of the dawn prayer before sunrise has caught it, and whoever catches one rak'ah of the afternoon prayer before sunset has caught it.
The two rak'ah before the dawn prayer are better than the world and everything in it.
Whoever prays the dawn prayer is under the protection of Allah.
Satan ties three knots at the back of your head when you sleep. Each is undone: by remembering Allah on waking, by wudu, and by prayer.
O Allah, bless my ummah in its early mornings.
No prayer is heavier upon the hypocrites than the night prayer and the dawn prayer. If they knew what is in them, they would come even crawling.
Whoever prays the night prayer in congregation, it is as though he prayed half the night; and whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation, as though he prayed the whole night.
Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in darkness: a complete light on the Day of Resurrection.
When the heat is intense, wait for it to cool before praying, for the fierceness of the heat is from the breath of the Fire.
Whoever keeps to four rak'ah before the midday prayer and four after it, Allah will forbid him to the Fire.
The gates of heaven are opened when the sun passes its zenith, and he liked a good deed of his to rise then.
Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as though he lost his family and his property.
Whoever abandons the afternoon prayer, his deeds are annulled.
On the day of the Trench he said: they kept us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer.
My ummah will remain upon the natural way as long as they do not delay the sunset prayer until the stars come out.
Pray two rak'ah before the sunset prayer. He said it three times, adding the third time: for whoever wishes.
We would pray the sunset prayer with him, and one of us could leave and still see where his arrow fell.
He disliked sleeping before the night prayer, and talking after it.
Were it not too hard on my ummah, I would have ordered them to delay the night prayer until a third of the night had passed.
Make the last of your prayer at night an odd number.
The first thing a servant will be brought to account for on the Day of Resurrection is his prayer. If it is sound, he has succeeded.
The key to prayer is purification, its opening is the takbir, and its closing is the taslim.
Between a man and disbelief and paganism stands the abandonment of prayer.
The covenant between us and them is prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved.
Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than a prayer offered alone.
If there were a river at your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain? That is the likeness of the five prayers: by them Allah wipes away sins.
The five daily prayers, and one Friday to the next, are an expiation for what lies between them, so long as the major sins are avoided.
Whoever goes to the mosque morning and evening, Allah prepares for him a welcome in Paradise every time he goes.
When the prayer is called, do not come to it running. Come walking, with calm and dignity; pray what you catch, and complete what you missed.
I asked which deed is most beloved to Allah. He said: prayer at its proper time.
Whoever forgets a prayer should pray it as soon as he remembers. There is no expiation for it but that.
Pray as you have seen me praying.
The nearest a servant comes to his Lord is while prostrating, so make much supplication then.
Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of the completeness of prayer.
Shall I tell you what erases sins and raises ranks? Completing the wudu despite discomfort, many steps to the mosque, and waiting for the next prayer after a prayer.
Allah has enjoined five prayers. Whoever observes them, neglecting none of their due, has a covenant with Allah that He will admit him to Paradise.
Instruct your children to pray when they are seven years old.
There is no servant who prays twelve voluntary rak'ah each day but that Allah builds for him a house in Paradise.
Between every call to prayer and the call to stand there is a prayer, for whoever wishes.
The angels ask forgiveness for one of you as long as he stays in the place where he prayed and has not broken his wudu.
When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rak'ah before he sits down.
